MMM.rationale: MMM is a deteriorating business with a stretched balance sheet and expensive valuation. Q1 2026 showed revenue of $6.03B (up only 1.3% YoY) but EPS collapsed 39.7% YoY to $1.23, with net income down 41.3%. Operating cash flow plunged 826.6% YoY to $574M. The balance sheet is severely strained with total equity of only $3.31B against total liabilities of $32.12B, implying a debt-to-equity ratio of ~9.7x. ROE of 0.845% is extremely low and deteriorating from 0.968% a year ago. Net margin compressed from 17.9% to 11.2%. Despite this fundamental deterioration, the stock trades at a P/E of 30.54x—near the top of its 365-day range (17.7-32.0x)—and P/B of 25.8x, both at or near all-time highs in the window. The stock has rallied 10.5% in the past quarter on no fundamental improvement. Management reaffirmed FY26 adjusted EPS guidance of $8.50-$8.70, but GAAP earnings are being crushed by litigation charges and restructuring costs. PFAS litigation remains a material overhang with potential for severe downside. The combination of deteriorating fundamentals, an extremely weak balance sheet, and peak valuation creates a highly unattractive risk/reward profile.
